description:
Organization Settings tab in the Promptless dashboard (https://app.gopromptless.ai/settings/org), covering the destination that src/content/docs/docs/work-the-queue/reviewing-prs.mdx sends readers to when it says a reader can change the comment trigger mode in Settings -> Organization Settings. Two things have to hold for that sentence to be usable: the tab has to be named Organization Settings and live at /settings/org, and the GitHub PR Comment Trigger Mode control has to be on that tab offering exactly the two modes the page's prose explains. This spec pins both, so a renamed tab, a moved route, or a renamed mode fails here instead of leaving readers on a page that does not hold the setting they were sent to change.

Scope, and what is deliberately left to another spec: nothing here touches the Environment Variables tab, the variables table, or the Add Variable form. Those controls belong to environment-variables-settings.spec.json, which already pins the bare-/settings redirect, the Environment Variables tab name, the Key Name and Value inputs, the Secret toggle, and the Add Variable submit button. The credential steps in src/content/docs/docs/get-the-most-out/screenshots.mdx name those same controls, so they are covered there rather than asserted twice.

NON-DESTRUCTIVE BY CONSTRUCTION. This spec never changes the test organization's configuration. It clicks nothing at all: no radio, no SAVE button, no tab. Every step is either a `goTo`, a `find` used purely as a wait, or a `runBrowserScript` probe that only reads the DOM -- none clicks, submits, assigns to a value or a `checked`, dispatches an event, or issues a request. That matters more here than on most pages, because each card on this tab writes a real organization-wide setting: clicking a GitHub PR Comment Trigger Mode radio and its SAVE would change how Promptless responds to comments on every PR in the test org. The spec therefore asserts the radios exist and are named as documented without selecting one, and asserts SAVE is present without pressing it. Which mode is currently selected is reported for debugging but is not asserted, because that is the org's live choice rather than a documented fact.

Authentication reuses the existing Clerk sign-in flow rather than a new one: the test sets `before` to login.spec.json, whose steps are prepended into this test's own browser context. That spec reads $PROMPTLESS_TEST_EMAIL and $PROMPTLESS_TEST_PASSWORD from .doc-detective/.env via the config's `loadVariables`, so no credential and no resolved internal host appears here. `before` resolves relative to this spec file because `relativePathBase` defaults to `file`; under `relativePathBase: cwd` Doc Detective skips this spec rather than failing it. login.spec.json opens with a `record` step that is unsupported headless and that skips when its fixed output path already exists, so that step often reports SKIPPED here -- a skipped step does not fail its context, since only an all-skipped context is itself skipped.

No test data prerequisite: the Organization Settings cards render from the org's own settings, so this spec passes against any signed-in test org without seeding anything.

Running it: neither config lists .doc-detective/tests/ in `input` (.doc-detective.json scans src/content/docs for inline tests), so pass this file explicitly -- `npx doc-detective -c .doc-detective.json -i .doc-detective/tests/organization-settings-pr-comment-trigger-mode.spec.json`. This spec is deliberately NOT added to .doc-detective.ci.json: Clerk-dependent flows were dropped from that config for being unstable, and reversing that is a maintainer call rather than this spec's to make.

URLs are absolute because the config's `origin` points at the docs site (https://promptless.ai), not the dashboard.

Assertion style follows homepage-product-switcher.spec.json and environment-variables-settings.spec.json: each `runBrowserScript` probe reports several related facts in one string, so a renamed control shows up as a readable diff instead of an opaque element-not-found. `find` steps are waits only and match text by regex, so incidental whitespace or a nested wrapper cannot fail a step whose job is just to know the page rendered; the exact documented names are asserted inside the probes instead. Names are compared against each element's own direct text with whitespace collapsed, because this page nests an option's helper sentence inside the same <label> as the option name -- a label's aggregated text therefore never equals the name on its own, and comparing aggregated text would either fail on every option or, with a substring test, let a helper sentence satisfy the assertion. Comparisons upper-case before matching wherever the UI applies a CSS text-transform: the card's save control has DOM text `Save`, rendered uppercase. `output` is a substring match on the serialized return value, so each probe keeps its asserted fields contiguous and puts diagnostic-only fields last.

tests.description: The page's link target: /settings/org serves the Settings tab whose name is Organization Settings, and that name is the one in the tab row rather than an abbreviation. Pins the two halves of the documented `Settings -> Organization Settings` path that can drift independently -- the route and the label -- and asserts the short form `Org Settings` is not what the tab is called, since a reader shown that name would not find it.

steps.description: Open the Organization Settings tab the docs link to
Wait for the Organization Settings tab to render, keyed on a card heading that only this tab has

The documented URL served this tab without redirecting elsewhere, the tab row offers the documented Organization Settings name as some element's own text, that name is the label on the link to /settings/org, and no tab is called the short form Org Settings

runBrowserScript.script: const own = (el) => Array.from(el.childNodes).filter((n) => n.nodeType === 3).map((n) => n.textContent).join(' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(); const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('body *')); const named = els.some((el) => own(el) === 'Organization Settings'); const shortForm = els.some((el) => own(el) === 'Org Settings'); const orgLink = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a[href]')).find((a) => new URL(a.href, window.location.origin).pathname === '/settings/org'); return ['path=' + window.location.pathname, 'orgTabName=' + (named ? 'present' : 'missing'), 'orgTabLink=' + (orgLink ? 'present' : 'missing'), 'orgTabLinkLabel=' + (orgLink ? ((orgLink.textContent || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim() === 'Organization Settings' ? 'Organization Settings' : 'other') : 'n-a'), 'shortFormOrgSettings=' + (shortForm ? 'present' : 'absent')].join(' ');
runBrowserScript.output: path=/settings/org orgTabName=present orgTabLink=present orgTabLinkLabel=Organization Settings shortFormOrgSettings=absent

steps.description: The GitHub PR Comment Trigger Mode card is on this tab and offers exactly the two modes the page's prose explains, as one radio group so they stay mutually exclusive, with its own save control. The card is scoped to the smallest ancestor of its heading that holds a radio without also swallowing another card's heading, so the neighbouring Slack Thread Reply Trigger Mode card -- which carries its own Require @promptless option, its own two radios, and its own Save -- cannot satisfy any of these assertions. If no such ancestor exists the probe reports cardScope=leaky and fails rather than asserting against a scope wide enough to be satisfied by the wrong card. Nothing is clicked: the radios are read, never selected, and the save control is asserted present, never pressed, so the org's setting is unchanged. selectedMode is diagnostic only -- which mode the org has chosen is its own live setting, not a documented fact.

runBrowserScript.script: const own = (el) => Array.from(el.childNodes).filter((n) => n.nodeType === 3).map((n) => n.textContent).join(' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(); const flat = (el) => (el.textContent || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(); const headings = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6')); const heading = headings.find((h) => flat(h) === 'GitHub PR Comment Trigger Mode'); if (!heading) return 'prCard=missing'; const others = headings.filter((h) => h !== heading && ['Default role for new members', 'Slack Thread Reply Trigger Mode', 'Suggestion Status Updates'].includes(flat(h))); let card = null; for (let el = heading.parentElement; el; el = el.parentElement) { if (!el.querySelector('input[type=radio]')) continue; card = others.some((h) => el.contains(h)) ? null : el; break; } if (!card) return 'prCard=present cardScope=leaky'; const radios = Array.from(card.querySelectorAll('input[type=radio]')); const groups = new Set(radios.map((r) => r.name || '')); const labelled = (name) => Array.from(card.querySelectorAll('*')).some((el) => own(el) === name) ? 'present' : 'missing'; const save = Array.from(card.querySelectorAll('button, input[type=submit]')).find((el) => (el.textContent || el.value || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().toUpperCase() === 'SAVE'); const selected = radios.find((r) => r.checked); return ['prCard=present', 'cardScope=isolated', 'modeRequireMention=' + labelled('Require @promptless'), 'modeListenAll=' + labelled('Listen to all PR comments (opt out with aside)'), 'prModeCount=' + radios.length, 'prModeGroups=' + groups.size, 'prCardSave=' + (save ? 'present' : 'missing'), 'selectedMode=' + (selected ? selected.value || 'unnamed' : 'none')].join(' ');
runBrowserScript.output: prCard=present cardScope=isolated modeRequireMention=present modeListenAll=present prModeCount=2 prModeGroups=1 prCardSave=present
